summary: This lecture tells of the mockery and pressure on the Prophet SAW at age 43 to 45 after the open call. The ustaz reads from Hamka's book Hamka Bercerita Sirah Nabi Muhammad SAW about the insults raining on him though he stayed gracious. The Quraysh chiefs pressed Abu Talib to stop him, but he said he would not stop even if the sun were placed in his right hand and the moon in his left, so Abu Talib kept protecting him. When his son Abdullah died, Quraysh rejoiced and said Muhammad was cut off, and Allah revealed Surah Al-Kawthar promising abundant good and declaring that his hater is the one cut off. The lecture closes with Mus'ab ibn Umair entering Islam and the torture of companions that would lead to the migration to Abyssinia.
keyPoints: Mockery upon mockery rained on the Prophet SAW, but he stayed gracious and called them to piety.
Abu Talib protected him like a passport in Mecca, and he refused to stop even if offered the sun and moon.
Quraysh rejoiced at the death of his son and said Muhammad was cut off.
Surah Al-Kawthar promises a river in paradise, many descendants and the largest community, and that his hater is the one cut off.
The Prophet's name is mentioned every moment in the world while his enemies' names have faded.

chapters.title: Opening and recap
chapters.summary: The ustaz recaps his story from birth to revelation and Surah Al-Alaq.

chapters.title: Secret and open calling
chapters.summary: Three years of secret calling, two banquets and the call on Mount Safa, which Abu Lahab cursed.

chapters.title: Hamka's book
chapters.summary: The ustaz introduces the book Hamka Bercerita Sirah Nabi Muhammad SAW and its author, Prof. Dr. Hamka.

chapters.title: Mockery upon mockery
chapters.summary: Hamka writes that mockery rained on him, and Surah Al-Masad was revealed in answer to Abu Lahab.

chapters.title: The hostile chiefs
chapters.summary: Abu Lahab, Abu Jahal and Abu Sufyan opposed him, pulled his collar, and Abu Lahab made his sons break their engagements.

chapters.title: Life after death
chapters.summary: Quraysh believed only bones remained after death, but he proclaimed an everlasting, unboring Hereafter.

chapters.title: Quraysh complain to Abu Talib
chapters.summary: They realised only Abu Talib protected him, like a passport in Mecca.

chapters.title: The delegation and demand
chapters.summary: They said the idol trade was threatened and told Abu Talib to summon him and make him stop.

chapters.title: The sun in my right hand
chapters.summary: He said he would not stop even if the sun and moon were placed in his hands, and Abu Talib was moved and kept protecting him.

chapters.title: Abdullah's death and Muhammad is cut off
chapters.summary: Quraysh including Abu Lahab and Al-Walid rejoiced at the death of his son and said Muhammad was cut off.

chapters.title: Surah Al-Kawthar
chapters.summary: Allah revealed the shortest surah to console him.

chapters.title: The meaning of Al-Kawthar
chapters.summary: Al-Kawthar means a river in paradise and a pond, many descendants through Fatimah, and the largest community.

chapters.title: Prayer, sacrifice and the hater cut off
chapters.summary: Allah told him to keep praying and sacrificing, and said his hater is cut off while his name is always mentioned.

chapters.title: Mus'ab and the migration to Abyssinia
chapters.summary: Mus'ab ibn Umair accepted Islam at the house of Al-Arqam, and the torture of companions would lead to migration to Abyssinia.

lessons.title: Staying gracious despite insult
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW did not reply harshly but called with love to piety.

lessons.title: There is life after death
lessons.body: We will meet again in paradise, an everlasting life.

lessons.title: Paradise is never dull
lessons.body: The delights of paradise never run out and never become dull.

lessons.title: Steadfast in calling
lessons.body: He would not stop until he won or was destroyed even when offered the impossible.

lessons.title: Do not rejoice at another's grief
lessons.body: When a friend loses a loved one we stop quarrelling and apologise, unlike Quraysh.

lessons.title: A good name lives on
lessons.body: The Prophet's name is mentioned every moment through the adhan, while his enemies' names are forgotten.

lessons.title: The largest community
lessons.body: The Prophet will have the most followers on the Day of Judgement compared to other prophets.

lessons.title: Keep praying and sacrificing
lessons.body: Allah told him to continue worship though mocked.
